sentences.text: Arthur Kipps was a young lawyer.
He was sent to a small village.
His job was to settle the estate of a deceased client.
The client was Mrs. Drablow.
She lived in a big, old house.
The house was called Eel Marsh House.
Arthur arrived at the village.
The people were quiet and strange.
They warned him about the house.
They said it was haunted.
Arthur did not believe them.
He thought ghosts were just stories.
Arthur went to Eel Marsh House.
It was far from the village.
The house was old and dark.
It was surrounded by marshes.
The air was cold and damp.
Arthur felt uneasy, but he had a job to do.
Inside the house, Arthur found many papers.
He started to read them.
As he worked, he heard strange noises.
He heard footsteps and whispers.
He saw shadows move.
Arthur was scared, but he stayed.
He needed to finish his work.
One night, Arthur saw a woman.
She was dressed in black.
Her face was pale and sad.
She looked at Arthur with angry eyes.
Then, she disappeared.
Arthur was shocked.
He asked the villagers about the woman.
They said she was the Woman in Black.
She was a ghost.
She was looking for revenge.
Arthur learned that the Woman in Black was Mrs. Drablow's sister.
She lost her child in the marshes.
She blamed Mrs. Drablow.
Now, she haunted the house.
She wanted to make everyone suffer.
Arthur was determined to finish his work.
He went back to the house.
The Woman in Black appeared again.
She screamed and cried.
Arthur felt cold and scared.
He tried to ignore her.
He worked quickly.
Finally, he finished his work.
Arthur left the house.
He felt relieved.
But the Woman in Black followed him.
She haunted him for the rest of his life.
Arthur never found peace.
He was always looking over his shoulder.
The Woman in Black was always there, watching and waiting.
